analysis.summary: Two high-severity functional bugs identified: arbitrary string casting to EventName enum will corrupt tracking data, and removal of CloudFront Function will break SPA routing causing 404s.

bugs.title: Invalid EventName casting from user-facing label
bugs.description: The code casts `linkLabel` (a user-facing display string like 'Learn More') to the `EventName` enum type. Since `linkLabel` can contain arbitrary text with spaces and different casing, this will send invalid event names to the tracking system, breaking analytics taxonomy.
bugs.risk: HIGH - Tracking events will be sent with invalid names (e.g., 'Learn More' instead of 'LEARN_MORE'), causing data loss or rejection by analytics pipelines.

bugs.title: CloudFront Function removal breaks SPA routing
bugs.description: The `cfFunction` CloudFront Function was removed entirely. This function handled critical URL rewriting: stripping base paths, appending 'index.html' to directory requests, and adding '.html' to extension-less paths. Without it, direct navigation to routes or page refreshes will result in 404 errors from S3.
bugs.risk: HIGH - Users refreshing the page or accessing deep links will receive 404 errors because S3 cannot resolve paths like `/page` to `/page.html` or `/` to `/index.html` automatically.

suggestions.suggestion: Map linkLabel values to valid EventName constants instead of casting arbitrary strings
suggestions.rationale: Maintain tracking taxonomy integrity by using a mapper object or switch statement to convert display labels to canonical event identifiers

suggestions.suggestion: Add SST StaticSite SPA fallback configuration or replace CloudFront Function
suggestions.rationale: If using SST StaticSite, ensure errorResponses or fallbackIndexFile are configured to handle SPA routing, or restore the CloudFront Function for URI rewriting

suggestions.suggestion: Verify BFF route migration is complete across all consumers
suggestions.rationale: The route paths changed from `/bff/*` to `/__app__/${featureAppName}/${target}/bff/*`; ensure no hardcoded clients or API gateways still call the old paths

notBugs.reason: The output path change in webpack.config.feature-app.ts aligns with the infrastructure changes and won't cause runtime errors if deployment artifacts match the new structure
The pathRewrite removal in webpack.config.web-app.ts is consistent with the BffApi.ts route changes; both now use the full path including baseUrl, so this is an intentional coordination
The functionName added to routes is ignored by enrichRoutes which constructs its own name; this is low severity as it doesn't cause runtime errors, just uses a different naming convention
